title: Concurrency policy guidance must not suggest a github.ref group; the opt-out is a per-run run_id group
answers: workflow run cancelled by another run of a different event
why does conftest tell me to add concurrency to my workflow
what concurrency group should I use in a workflow that must not be cancelled
release-note workflow cancelled by a later event
body:
Symptom: a workflow run is cancelled or superseded by a run from another event (e.g. a later issue_comment or workflow_run) that shares its concurrency group.
Root cause: .github/policy.rego:deny_workflow_without_concurrency used to recommend the group '${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.ref }}', which is unsafe for pull_request_target, issue_comment, issues and workflow_run. The guidance contributed to the release-note.yml cancellation bug fixed in #25624.
Fix pattern: when the policy message or a workflow needs an opt-out from grouping, show the complete block `concurrency: {group: ${{ github.run_id }}, cancel-in-progress: false}`; do not offer the github.ref group as the standard.
Constraints: a per-run unique group only stops concurrency-based cancellation and serialization. It does not promise that a run completes, since runs can still queue for runner capacity or be cancelled for other reasons; scope the wording to 'allow each run to proceed independently' (the reviewed wording).
applies: The deny message text in .github/policy.rego and any guidance about concurrency groups for workflows in .github/workflows/*.yml.
says: Release notes were not generated after someone commented on the release pull request.
The automated release notes task was cancelled unexpectedly before finishing its publication step.
Ensure release note generation runs independently without being aborted by newer comment activity.
The pipeline policy check suggests a concurrency setting that cancels runs across events.
search: Workflow concurrency policy guidance in .github/policy.rego must recommend a per-run group: ${{ github.run_id }} with cancel-in-progress: false instead of a github.ref-based group. The rule deny_workflow_without_concurrency previously suggested '${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.ref }}', which caused workflow runs such as release-note.yml to be cancelled by subsequent pull_request_target, issue_comment, issues, or workflow_run events. Policy text must scope wording to allow each run to proceed independently, as unique run_id groups stop only concurrency cancellation and serialization without guaranteeing run completion against runner queueing or other cancellations.
